issues.description: The exercise specifies an interface named 'Milkable' with the method signature String messageOnMilk() (problem statement/UML and template usage), but the solution code defines an interface named 'Dairy' (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Dairy.java) and implements that in Goat and Seal. Meanwhile the solution repository also contains an empty Milkable.java file (no interface declaration). This naming mismatch means the conceptual 'milkable' interface is referred to as 'Milkable' in the problem and template but implemented as 'Dairy' in the solution; students implementing 'Milkable' will not match the solution's classes, and automated checks or examples that expect Milkable may fail or confuse students.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the interface name consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix: rename the solution's Dairy interface to Milkable (file Dairy.java -> Milkable.java), ensure it declares String messageOnMilk(); update Goat.java and Seal.java to implement Milkable, and remove the stray/empty Milkable.java file. Alternatively, update the problem statement/template to use 'Dairy' everywhere, but renaming the solution to 'Milkable' preserves the original exercise wording and prevents student confusion.
